items.summary: The Board of Supervisors convened for roll call and the Pledge of Allegiance. Supervisor Dorsey was formally excused from the meeting due to jury duty by a unanimous roll call vote. The Board also acknowledged the unceded ancestral homeland of the Ramaytush Ohlone people.
The Clerk presented routine communications regarding viewing options, public comment procedures, and disability accommodations for the Board of Supervisors meeting.
The Board considered the consent agenda consisting of items 1 through 10. The consent agenda ordinances were finally passed and resolutions adopted following a unanimous roll call vote.

The Board approved items 1 through 10 on the consent agenda by roll call vote. The package included capital improvement certificates of participation not to exceed $65 million, a $2,828,000 settlement with the Coalition on Homelessness, settlements with TPx Communications, SEIU Local 1021, and several other litigation settlements and unlitigated claims.

The Board considered an ordinance authorizing a partial settlement of litigation against members of the Raymond Sackler family, securing $8 million to $12 million over 15 years for opioid abatement. The item was called together with Item 12 and passed without objection.

The Board considered an ordinance approving a settlement of approximately $15.4 million in a lawsuit against AT&T Corp. and Pacific Bell Telephone Company concerning access line taxes under the California False Claims Act. The ordinance was finally passed without objection.

The Board considered an ordinance to amend the Planning Code to waive certain development impact fees in the Market and Octavia Area Plan for 26 approved pipeline projects. Supervisor Chan noted concerns about forfeiting revenue for affordable housing and infrastructure but supported the amended compromise, while Supervisor Fielder opposed the measure as an unnecessary developer giveaway that undermines the city's affordable housing mandate. The ordinance passed on first reading by an 8-2 vote.

speakers.name: Connie Chan
speakers.quote: NOW WE'RE EXPECTING A ROUGHLY ABOUT $81 MILLION OF FEE WAIVER BUT THAT'S AT THE EXPENSE OF AFFORDABLE HOUSING INFRASTRUCTURE AND AS WELL AS COMMUNITY FACILITIES.

speakers.name: Jackie Fielder
speakers.quote: WITH THIS ORDINANCE WE WILL BE FORFEITING $81 MILLION IN LOST REVENUE FOR COMMUNITIES THAT IS LOSING OVER $47 MILLION OF REVENUE FOR COMMUNITY INFRASTRUCTURE AND OVER 33 MILLION IN AFFORDABLE HOUSING FEES.

items.summary: The Board considered an ordinance appropriating $400,000 from General City Responsibility and $14,303 from DPW for District 7 neighborhood projects and services, including curb ramps, sidewalk repairs, school blacktop and murals, and Ocean Avenue art pop-ups. The ordinance passed on first reading by a unanimous roll call vote.

The Board adopted a resolution approving modification number five to an airport professional services agreement with AGS, Inc. for International Terminal Building Phase 2 project management support services, increasing the contract by $2.85 million to an amount not to exceed $12.5 million.

The Board adopted a resolution authorizing the Recreation and Parks Department to accept an in-kind grant valued at approximately $300,000 from the Union Square Alliance for sound system improvements at the Union Square Plaza stage.

The Board adopted a resolution approving a first amendment to a Port lease with the YMCA SF for Building 49 at Crane Cove Park, adjusting rent credit provisions and providing $150,000 in new rent credits to offset unexpected structural repair costs.

The Board considered an ordinance amending the Business and Tax Regulations Code to reduce the gross receipts tax and homelessness gross receipts tax rate for telecommunications business activities. The ordinance passed on first reading without objection.

The Board adopted a resolution granting a behested payment waiver to allow designated city officials and the Fire Chief to solicit donations from public and private entities to fund cancer screenings for eligible Fire Department personnel.

The Board passed on first reading an ordinance amending the Subdivision Code to establish procedures for resale prices, capital improvements, and conveyances of below-market-rate condominium conversion units.

The Board passed on first reading an ordinance amending the Building Code to remove certain local requirements regarding commercial lighting, rooftop mechanical penthouses, and driveway and sidewalk load limits.
The Board passed on first reading an ordinance amending the Health Code to clarify enhanced ventilation standards for sensitive use developments and major renovations.
The Board passed on first reading an ordinance ordering the summary vacation and quitclaim of a public service easement at 112 Kensington Way for $20,000.
The Board adopted a resolution granting revocable permission to Bridge Potrero Community Associates LLC to maintain encroachments in the public right-of-way for the Potrero HOPE SF project.

The Board adopted a resolution urging a preventative, data-driven inter-agency approach to ending severe and fatal traffic collisions on San Francisco streets, titled the San Francisco Street Safety Act.
The Board approved a motion appointing Amanda Pyle to the Children and Families First Commission for a term ending October 8, 2026.
The Board approved the mayoral appointment of Jordan Wilson to the Entertainment Commission for a term ending July 1, 2029.
The Board approved the mayoral reappointment of Bianca Neumann to the Building Inspection Commission for a term ending July 1, 2027.
The Board approved Board President Rafael Mandelman's nomination to reappoint Alysabeth Alexander-Tut to the Building Inspection Commission for a term ending July 1, 2027.

Supervisor Bilal Mahmood and Board President Rafael Mandelman commended Richard Beale in honor of National Recovery Month for his 30 years of sobriety and leadership in unhoused, reentry, and addiction recovery services. Beale addressed the Board, thanking advocates and calling for more treatment beds, drug-free housing, and the closure of open-air drug markets.

speakers.name: Bilal Mahmood
speakers.quote: FOR NEARLY THREE DECADES, RICHARD HAS WORKED TO ENSURE THAT THE VOICES OF THOSE TOO OFTEN LEFT OUT INDIVIDUALS EXPERIENCING HOMELESSNESS THOSE LIVING WITH ADDICTION AND THOSE RETURNING FROM INCARCERATION ARE NOT JUST HEARD BUT SEEN

speakers.name: Rafael Mandelman
speakers.quote: I FEEL LIKE I HAVE, YOU KNOW, BEEN A WITNESS OVER THESE LAST SEVEN YEARS OF A REAL TRANSFORMATION IN THE CONVERSATION ABOUT RECOVERY AND HOW WE PRIORITIZE RECOVERY AS A CITY

items.summary: During Roll Call for Introductions, supervisors introduced new resolutions and memorial adjournments. Supervisor Melgar introduced a resolution designating Good Neighbor Week. Supervisor Sherrill recognized the upcoming Chuseok Festival, Supervisor Walton honored the life and legacy of Jackie Cohen, and Supervisor Engardio introduced an adjournment in memory of community ambassador Quang Cuong.

speakers.name: Myrna Melgar
speakers.quote: IN 2023 THE US SURGEON GENERAL DECLARED LONELINESS A PUBLIC HEALTH CRISIS. AND NOW AS WE FACE A SOCIETY THAT IS GROWING MORE ANXIOUS WITH POLITICAL DIVISIVENESS AND TOXICITY, WE NEED TO CONNECT WITH EACH OTHER FOR THE SAKE OF OUR SHARED HUMANITY.

speakers.name: Stephen Sherrill
speakers.quote: I JUST WANTED TO THANK SUPERVISOR MELGAR FOR INTRODUCING THE STREET SAFETY ACT. I THINK IT IS A CRITICAL NEXT STEP IN OUR JOURNEY TO ENSURING THE STREETS ARE SAFE

speakers.name: Shamann Walton
speakers.quote: COLLEAGUES TODAY I HAVE AND MORE AM TO HONOR THE LIFE AND LEGACY OF JACQUELINE. KNOWN AS JACKIE COHEN, A PROUD NATIVE SAN FRANCISCAN AND BELOVED MEMBER OF THE BAYVIEW HUNTERS POINT COMMUNITY WHERE SHE LIVED FOR OVER 40 YEARS.

speakers.name: Joel Engardio
speakers.quote: TODAY I ASK THAT WE ADJOURN THIS MEETING IN MEMORY OF KWANG QUIN. A BELOVED COMMUNITY AMBASSADOR IN THE OUTER SUNSET.

items.summary: Members of the public addressed the Board on general matters not on the published agenda, including Good Neighbor Week activities, death penalty abolition, parcel taxes, government surveillance, and community grievances regarding city commissions.

speakers.name: Public commenter
speakers.quote: I'M JULIA CARESS THE FOUNDER OF SAN FRANCISCO GOOD NEIGHBOR WEEK AND ONE OF THE USF NONPROFIT INNOVATORS THIS YEAR.

speakers.name: Public commenter
speakers.quote: AND I URGE EVERYONE TO PLEASE CALL ON GOVERNOR NEWSOM TO COMMUTE EVERYBODY FROM OUR DEATH ROW.

speakers.name: Public commenter
speakers.quote: I'M HERE AGAIN TO TALK ABOUT PARCEL TAXES BECAUSE NOBODY SEEMS TO KNOW WHAT PARCEL TAXES REALLY ARE ABOUT.

public_comment_themes: Complaints about Behavioral Health Commission and Sunshine Ordinance Task Force

items.summary: The Board considered items on the For Adoption Without Committee Reference agenda. Items 32, 33, 35, 36, and 37 were adopted unanimously by roll call vote, while Item 34 was severed for separate consideration.

The Board adopted items 32, 33, 35, 36, and 37 without committee reference by roll call vote. The package included a resolution urging Governor Newsom to commute all death sentences in California and a 90-day extension for Planning Commission review of family dwelling unit definitions.

The Board severed and considered Item 34, a resolution proclaiming September 15 through October 15, 2025 as Latinx Heritage Month in San Francisco. Supervisors Melgar and Fielder spoke in celebration of the community's cultural, social, and economic contributions to the city, and the resolution was adopted without objection.

speakers.name: Myrna Melgar
speakers.quote: COLLEAGUES I AM HONORED TO INTRODUCE A RESOLUTION PROCLAIMING SEPTEMBER 15TH THROUGH OCTOBER 15TH 2025 AS LATIN HERITAGE MONTH IN THE CITY AND COUNTY OF SAN FRANCISCO.

speakers.name: Jackie Fielder
speakers.quote: SO I AM I'M VERY PROUD TO BE MEXICAN-AMERICAN, BE THE FIRST LATINA WOMAN TO REPRESENT DISTRICT NINE, MY GRANDPARENTS ON MY MOTHER'S SIDE WERE FROM MONTERREY, MEXICO.

items.summary: The Board of Supervisors adjourned in memory of Raven Sorrel, Jackie Cohen, and Quang Cuong.
